newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Telecinco pushes changes to TV laws.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Telecinco pushes changes to TV laws.

text.p: Spanish television broadcaster Gestevision Telecinco SA urged on Tuesday that laws regulating television be changed so that it could list on the bourse.
"We would like this country's laws to allow us to list on the bourse as soon as possible," the chief executive of the private TV broadcaster, Maurizio Carlotti, told journalists.
Carlotti said TV chains needed to finance themselves which made a bourse listing or issue of convertible bonds, essential. Neither of these possibilities is legal in Spain.
Group president Alejandro Echevarria said Telecinco had taken out a 15 billion peseta loan to finance strategic investments.
Telecinco is owned 25 percent by Italian group Fininvest's Mediaset and 25 percent by Germany's Kirch, with the remainder controlled predominantly by Spanish investors.
